title: Lesson 23: Quality Gates and Review: Who Checks the Work, and What They Check For
description: Building quality gates into an agent delivery: why the builder cannot be the checker, writing testable acceptance criteria, routing a reviewer verdict back to the implementer, and attaching evidence to every handoff.

questions.question: Why must a reviewer be someone other than the builder?
options: Because reviewing takes time the builder cannot spare on delivery
Because shared context produces shared blind spots in the work
Because the reviewer is usually more senior than the builder
Because a second pass by the same author takes longer to complete
questions.explanation: Builder blindness is universal: a reviewer who shares the builder's session, memory, and assumptions reads the artifact the same way and misses the same gap.

questions.question: What distinguishes decision review from artifact review?
options: Artifact review requires a human while decision review can be scripted
Artifact review is done by the builder while decision review is done by the client
Artifact review happens after delivery while decision review happens before
Artifact review checks output while decision review judges approach
questions.explanation: Artifact review is mechanical and should be automated; decision review asks whether the approach was right and is where a human reviewer earns their place.

questions.question: How should a reviewer reject a candidate?
options: Route it back to the implementer with a reason
Block the card so the blocked column records the rejection
Leave a comment and let the implementer decide whether to act
Reopen the task in triage so a new scope is written
questions.explanation: A verdict is a routable decision: rejection returns the work to the implementer with a reason, while block is reserved for real escalation, since using it for rejection burns the signal.
